contract_plain_english: For any positive k and finite floating-point inputs with b_k nonzero, evaluating (c-sum a_i b_i)/b_k in round-to-nearest arithmetic, in any summation-tree order and without underflow or overflow, yields a computed y_hat that satisfies an exact coefficientwise backward identity with c unchanged and every coefficient bounded by k*u. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Lemma 4.1 statement; PDF p. 3, printed p. 686; anchor: whatever-order and unperturbed-c discussion] If b_k=1, every bound is (k-1)u, and the proof constructs sign-aligned witnesses from one scalar residual epsilon. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Lemma 4.1 proof] The constants contain no O(u^2) term and require no smallness condition on k*u. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: subsection 4.1 opening paragraph]

source_evidence.observation: For positive k, floating-point a_1,...,a_{k-1}, b_1,...,b_k, c with b_k nonzero, the computed value y_hat of (c-sum a_i b_i)/b_k admits coefficients theta_k^(0),...,theta_k^(k-1) satisfying the displayed exact identity and absolute bounds ku; when b_k=1, all bounds improve to (k-1)u.

For b_k=1, the proof first bounds |y_hat-y| by (k-1)u times |y_hat| plus the absolute product sum, represents the residual using one real epsilon, and defines epsilon^(0)=-sign(y_hat)epsilon and epsilon^(i)=-sign(a_i b_i)epsilon.
The paper interprets whatever order as any rooted binary summation tree over c and the product terms; it also emphasizes that c remains unperturbed in these backward identities.

The improved bounds are stated to have no dimension restriction and no quadratic terms, and to hold for round-to-nearest arithmetic with any radix, tie-breaking rule, and summation order when underflow and overflow are absent.

source_evidence.anchor: Sections 2.1-2.2, floating-point set and standard model
source_evidence.observation: F is a finite floating-point set with radix beta, precision p, and exponent range; rounding is to a nearest member with arbitrary tie breaking, and u=(1/2)beta^(1-p).

statement.algorithm_linkage: The lemma concerns separate floating-point evaluation of the product terms, their subtraction/summation in any binary-tree order, and finally division by nonzero b_k; b_k=1 removes that division. It is the coefficientwise backward representation later used for substitution and LU analysis. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 686; anchor: whatever-order convention; PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Lemma 4.1 and following application]
binders: k is a positive natural number. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Lemma 4.1 statement]
a_1,...,a_{k-1}, b_1,...,b_{k-1}, b_k, and c are members of F. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Lemma 4.1 statement]

The backward identity has real witnesses theta_k^(i) indexed by i=0,...,k-1. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 686; anchor: real theta coefficients in (1.5); PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Lemma 4.1 identity]
conclusions: There exist coefficients such that b_k*y_hat*(1+theta_k^(0)) = c - sum_{i=1}^{k-1} a_i*b_i*(1+theta_k^(i)). [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Lemma 4.1 displayed identity]
|theta_k^(i)| <= k*u for every i=0,...,k-1. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Lemma 4.1 displayed coefficient bound]
If b_k=1, so no division is performed, the same identity has witnesses satisfying |theta_k^(i)| <= (k-1)u for every i. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: sentence following Lemma 4.1 identity]
For b_k=1, |y_hat-y| <= (k-1)u*(|y_hat|+sum_{i=1}^{k-1}|a_i b_i|). [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: first displayed bound in the proof of Lemma 4.1]

For b_k=1, the proof chooses epsilon in R with y_hat-y=epsilon*(|y_hat|+sum|a_i b_i|), |epsilon| <= (k-1)u, then sets epsilon^(0)=-sign(y_hat)epsilon and epsilon^(i)=-sign(a_i b_i)epsilon; these witnesses yield y_hat*(1+epsilon^(0))=c-sum a_i b_i*(1+epsilon^(i)). [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: sign-aligned coefficient construction]
The nonunit-denominator case is asserted to follow analogously from Corollary 3.2 with b=b_k, n=k, x_1=c, and x_{i+1}=-a_i b_i. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: final sentence of Lemma 4.1 proof]
constants_and_indexing: The sum and product perturbations use indices i=1,...,k-1, while theta_k^(0) is attached to b_k*y_hat. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Lemma 4.1 identity]
